messages:
jess-support: Hey team, escalating an embedding issue from ACME customer. They say embedding endpoint returns mixed dimensions across requests and their pipeline crashes (expecting 1024 but sometimes gets 1536). They tested with quantization profiles (fp16 vs int8) and batching. Repro steps they gave below. Customer also hit a big rerun which spiked usage and they asked about credits. :warning:

Customer repro (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \\  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\  -d '{"model":"embed-prod-v1","input":["hello","world"],"quantization":"int8","batch_size":8}'
```
Response snippet: (they pasted)
```
{ "data": [ {"embedding": [/* length 1536 */] }, {"embedding": [/* length 1536 */] } ], "usage": {...} }
```
They say when they switch to fp16 it returns 1024 and similarities look correct. They also see `x-embed-dim: 1536` in response headers intermittently. Root cause unknown.

sarah-ml: thanks Jess. Can you paste the exact model id the customer used (not just "embed-prod-v1") and the request-id/routing headers if available? We need to know if different model variants were used. Also, did they set a model pin or rely on default routing?

jess-support: customer sent: model: "embed-large-1024" in body, no explicit pin param. Request-IDs: r-abs1234, r-abs1235 (two consecutive calls). I asked them for the full response headers; they sent back `x-served-model: embed-XL-1536-int8` for one request and `x-served-model: embed-L-1024-fp16` for another.

omar-ops: @sarah-ml @michael-ml that header is suspicious — looks like smart routing/fallback kicked in and routed one of their requests to a different model family (1536 dim) when the preferred int8 runtime wasn't available. We have a routing policy that allows cost-tier fallback; if the int8 quantized shard isn't available, it can route to a higher-capacity variant. That would explain dimension mismatch.

michael-ml: this matches my gut. Important: quantization (fp16 vs int8) shouldn't change embedding vector length. If dimension differs it's because a different model architecture/variant was served (e.g., embed-XL vs embed-L). Check model metadata: which model IDs map to which embedding dims.

luis-engineer: quick mitigation: ask the customer to pin model version or set fallback policy to none. E.g., in their request body include `"model_pin": "embed-L-1024@v3"` or `"routing.fallback": "none"` to enforce failure rather than silent fallback. Also we should surface a warning in the response when a fallback to an incompatible-dim model occurs. Right now only x-served-model exists which is easy to miss.

jess-support: I forwarded pin example and a small repro script to the customer. They confirmed pinning makes it stable (always 1024). They asked why switching `quantization` changed the served model when they thought quantization was just an execution detail.

sarah-ml: explanation snippet to pass back to customer (short):
- model architecture determines embedding dimension.
- quantization profile is an execution/runtime optimization for a model binary. If an exact quantized binary for a specific model/version isn't available in the requested region/instance, the router can select a compatible-but-different architecture with a different embedding head (hence different dim).

- if you need strict dims: pin the model id+version or set `routing.fallback: none` in the request.

omar-ops: logs from routing for r-abs1234/5 show: `route_decision: primary:embed-L-1024-int8 -> resource_unavailable -> fallback:embed-XL-1536-int8` (so it actually chose XL-int8). Odd that switching to fp16 returned 1024 — that implies an available fp16 binary existed for the L model but not int8. We'll open a capacity ticket for int8 on the L fleet.

michael-ml: added: we should also check if our model catalog metadata exposes dims clearly via GET /v1/models/:id; customer devs often expect embedding dims to be stable across quantizations — ops shd not silently swap arch. Suggested API change: return `x-embedding-dim` header and an explicit `served_model_id` in response body.

luis-engineer: repro script I gave customer (Python) — they ran it with batch_size=1 vs batch_size=16, found the dim flip only happened under batch_size > 8 with int8. My hypothesis: when int8 capacity is constrained we route batched requests to a single larger instance that only has the XL int8 binary available. So batching increases the chance of routing to XL. That would explain batch/throughput correlation.

jess-support: customer also reported a similarity regression: cosine(fp16 vs int8) dropped from ~0.98 to ~0.76 when comparing same texts across the two dims (but that comparison is invalid across dims). We told them to compare same-dim vectors only. They flagged the billing spike from reruns — finance looped in (cc:billing) to look at credits.

omar-ops: action items: (1) Runtime: prioritize bringing int8 binary up on L fleet in region eu-west-1 (owner: @omar-ops) — ticket RUNTIME-8943. (2) API: consider surfacing `served_model_id` and `embedding_dim` in response to prevent confusion (owner: @michael-ml). (3) Support: offer the customer a one-time usage credit for rerun (owner: @jess-support).

michael-ml: short-term workaround to recommend: force `quantization: fp16` OR pin `model_id@version` OR set `routing.fallback: none`. Example request we gave them:
```json
{
  "model": "embed-L-1024@v3",
  "input": ["a","b"],
  "quantization": "int8",
  "routing": {"fallback":"none"}
}
```
If fallback is none and the int8 binary isn't available you'll get a 503 instead of a silent different-dim response — which is better for deterministic pipelines.

luis-engineer: FYI deploy-bot just posted a recent deploy that may have affected int8 rollout in eu-west-1. Deploy logs: `deploy embed-int8 L fleet -> partial -> rollback at 03:12Z` (looks like some nodes never finished). I'm going to assign an infra rollback verification.

deploy-bot: [deploy log] deploy_id: d-2026-11-09-109, status: partial_rollback, affected_clusters: embed-int8-l-eu-west

jess-support: I'll loop customer back with the explanation and the pin+fallback workaround. Also will inform them we've opened RUNTIME-8943 and FIN-2982 (credit review).

sarah-ml: nice. Long-term we should document: "Quantization may influence routing to different model binaries; embedding dimension is model-architecture specific." Add to docs and change API to include served model id + dim. Create a short blurb for the support KB.

michael-ml: I'll draft the API change RFC and tag runtime and infra. Expect preliminary proposal by EOW.

jess-support: thanks all, customer is relieved to have a reproducible mitigation. Marking this thread resolved-for-now, will re-open if more dim mismatches show up. :thumbsup:
